title: Emergency Evacuation Planning
short_description: Compute shortest safe evacuation corridor hops, evaluate fire containment zones, broadcast incident alerts tier-by-tier, and audit ward tree hierarchies.
real_world_context: Hospital infrastructure must maintain rigorous emergency disaster evacuation protocols to safeguard immobile patients, medical personnel, and critical life-support apparatus during fires, gas leaks, or seismic events. Hospital safety management platforms model facility layouts as corridor networks and administrative command trees. During an evacuation, navigation systems use Breadth-First Search (BFS) to find the shortest unweighted corridor route from compromised wards to safe exterior exits, Depth-First Search (DFS) to map isolated fire-barrier compartments, Tree BFS to broadcast code-red incident instructions down chain-of-command tiers, and Tree DFS to audit hierarchical ward evacuation dependencies.
learning_objectives: Apply Breadth-First Search (BFS) on unweighted corridor graphs to find the minimum number of transitions to a safe hospital exit.
Use Depth-First Search (DFS) to identify and inspect all reachable rooms within an isolated fire barrier compartment.
Execute Tree BFS (level-order traversal) to coordinate tier-by-tier emergency alert broadcasts across incident response hierarchies.
Apply Tree DFS to calculate hierarchy depth and dependent sub-ward capacity across hospital emergency trees.
Identify critical structural bottlenecks (bridges) in a corridor network using Tarjan's bridge-finding algorithm to ensure evacuation redundancy.
